evidence.V1: The top view clearly shows an L corner, but the front and silhouette read as a plain tall block or pillar. Course joints barely notch the outline and the corner is not identifiable at 64 px from the front.
evidence.V2: Plinth course, 4 stone courses and a coping cap give some layers, but every stone is the same rectangle in a stack bond, so the medium/small tier is repetitive.
evidence.V3: Blocks are stacked in straight stack bond with a continuous vertical joint running up the corner. There is no running bond, no interlocking quoins and no size variation, so it reads stiff and grid-like.
evidence.V4: Close outer-corner and end-x studio shots show consistent small chamfers on every stone that catch light along the top edges.
evidence.V5: Close-ups are clean, with no pinches, seams or z-fighting on the stone faces. The end-y close-up shows only a flat featureless face (uninformative but artifact-free).
evidence.V6: One stone hue in about 3 values (dark plinth, mid and light stones). Brick and sandstone colourways keep the same discipline.
evidence.V7: 620 tris against a module target of 800, so it is under target.
evidence.V8: Chamfers and single vertex-colour material match, but the wall ends and inner faces are plain untreated dark slabs with no stone detail, and there is no timber/gold/plaster accent typical of the modular kit.
evidence.V9: Studio line: Anchored, Box fidelity, CanTouch off, Color white, SmoothPlastic, pivot at grid corner on a 2-stud grid. T1 on_grid, inside and touches_floor are all true. Correct.

top_fixes: Interlock the corner with alternating quoin stones (running bond) instead of one continuous vertical joint up the corner
Vary stone sizes and stagger courses so the faces are not a repeating stack-bond grid
Give the exposed wall ends and inner faces stone/course detail or a finished cap. Also verify flush self-tiling (the tiling.tiles list is empty)
